title: Irving Mills as manager
summary: Mills managed from the Kentucky Club and traveled with them first class.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Now, when did Irving Mills begin to manage the band?
He managed us at the Kentucky Club.
When you were at the Kentucky Club.

At the Kentucky Club. He become our official manager when in fact, he managed us when we went from the Kentucky Club too, to Cotton Club. He handled a lot of recordings for Duke's songs, because he never managed no band. But he had a big publishing house at 49th and Broadway in the Brill Building. He used to come here us all the time and he got those ideas and he -- that's when he said I am going to take you all and manage you. He didn't have no band. Later on he had Ina Ray Hutton's band, that's all.
What kind of a guy was he?

Irving Mills. He was blue white diamond. He was the guy. He was the guy. He traveled with us. Everything first class, everytime you look around, he said 'I better get you guys another set of uniforms'. Everytime we opened up, he had boutonnaire flowers. He was there to see everything is perfect. In fact, I told you before, every show we had a different uniform from top to bottom.
